title: Dispatches from Discharge Hell: A 25-Part Series on the Patterns Nobody Warns You About
target_keyword: Over 25 posts, I walk through the recurring patterns that unfold across hundreds of catastrophic discharges. These aren't isolated incidents. They're structural. Built into the system. Repeated so predictably I can predict the trajectory from the preadmission assessment.

title: Part 1: The Family Readiness Mismatch
target_keyword: The mother expected four months. We had three weeks. What the system calls inpatient rehab and what families expect are measured in completely different currencies.

title: Part 2: The Payer-Driven Discharge Timeline
target_keyword: Day 22. The patient can't swallow. Can't transfer independently. Can't tell you their own name. Day 23. Insurance wants to know why we haven't discharged.

title: Part 3: The Ghost SNF
target_keyword: We called six skilled nursing facilities on a Tuesday. Two said yes on the phone. By end of day, both had determined the patient was not appropriate for their level of care. A verbal acceptance is worth nothing until the patient is physically in the building.

title: Part 4: The DME Delivery Black Hole
target_keyword: We ordered the hospital bed two weeks ago. Week three, discharge day: the bed is ready, but the pressure-relief cushion is delayed. Those three days cost more than all the equipment combined.

title: Part 5: The Home Health Illusion
target_keyword: The family heard 'home health' and exhaled. Finally, a plan that sounded like help. A nurse visits twice a week for 45 minutes. Between those visits, the family is alone 23 hours a day. That gap is the single biggest source of post-discharge frustration in catastrophic care.

title: Part 6: The Faith-Function Tension
target_keyword: The family said God would heal their father. The medical team would not provide a clear prognosis and the insurance medical director said his brain injury was incompatible with meaningful recovery. Both of these things were true to the people who said them. And we were the ones in the middle, trying to build a discharge plan that honored both.

title: Part 7: Funny How That Works
target_keyword: 4:47 PM on a Friday. Denial of continued stay. Effective immediately. The attending physician left at 4:00. The utilization review office closes at 5:00. The appeal deadline is 72 hours. If you're counting, that burns through the entire weekend. Funny how that works.

title: Part 8: The Complexity-Admission Mismatch
target_keyword: We take the cases nobody else will. The spreadsheet says we need to turn beds over in 21 days. Both statements are true. Neither one acknowledges the other. The hospital wants a high CMI for reputation and a low length of stay for revenue. The case manager and social worker are asked to make both true simultaneously.

title: Part 9: The Difficult Conversation Industrial Complex
target_keyword: The patient has been here 18 days. Disorder of consciousness. Minimal response. Everyone has written the truth. Nobody has said it out loud. This is the Difficult Conversation Industrial Complex: a system where everyone agrees the family deserves honest information, and no one's job description makes them the person who delivers it.

title: Part 10: Perverse Incentives by Design
target_keyword: Every person in the discharge ecosystem is doing their job correctly. The insurance company denies coverage. The SNF refuses the complex patient. The DME vendor works within timelines. The hospital pushes for faster discharge. Everyone is responding rationally to their incentives. The patient is the only one whose incentives aren't in the model.

title: Part 11: It Depends on Who Shows Up
target_keyword: Family presence is the single strongest predictor of discharge destination in catastrophic care. Stronger than diagnosis. Stronger than insurance. Stronger than functional status.

title: Part 12: Not Our Problem Anymore
target_keyword: When the patient doesn't fit any department's criteria, they become a hot potato passed between units. Nobody is wrong. The system is just broken.

title: Part 14: I Already Called Them
target_keyword: The upstream reroute: the invisible work case managers do before the meeting starts. Calling the SNF before the referral. Prepping the physician before the family hears it. None of it shows up in the metrics.

title: Part 13: We Don't Do Out-of-Area
target_keyword: Houston is a destination hospital city. Getting in is the easy part. Getting home — back to a zip code with no SNFs, no neuro home health, and one DME vendor closed on weekends — is where discharge planning gets hard.

title: What the Neighbors Will Think: When Social Shame Becomes a Discharge Barrier
target_keyword: A mother refuses to take her minimally conscious daughter home after anoxic brain injury, despite clinical consensus. The barrier isn't denial—it's the fear of being laughed at by her community.

title: The Other Woman: When Unconventional Family is Your Best Discharge Plan
